description: The rotation board: 60 ETFs ranked wide to narrow against their parent index, with the $10B+ names carrying each move. For "where is money going?" across the whole market rather than inside one segment. Analyst plan or higher.

horizon.description: The lens: the ETF sort column (d1 / w1 / m1), the vs_parent band (1 / 2 / 4 pp) and the evidence ages (breakout signals and spikes inside 1 / 5 / 5 sessions; 52-week extremes within 1 / 5 / ~32). Default week. Every derived number is recomputed for it.

include_evidence.description: Include each stock row's `evidence[]` (the non-breakout facts with their values and ages). Default true; `sources[]` and `hits` remain either way.

include_history.description: Include the history arrays: each ETF and stock row's ~40-point 100-session [unix_seconds, close, sma50, sma150] `trend`, `cycle.activityLine` (the composite activity series), `cycle.activity[].series`, `cycle.clock.path` and `cycle.outlook.curve` / `curveShifted`. Default false.

include_notes.description: Include the static `signalKinds` catalogue (Breakout Moves' block, ~1k tokens, byte-identical on every response). Default false — each row's `signals[].kind` ids are self-describing and describe_dataset('get_breakout_moves') carries the same catalogue; the dashboard passes true for its pill labels.

lane.description: Which money direction to keep — descriptive (the sign of the evidence), not a trade list. Default both.

layer.description: Keep only ETF rows of this width layer. Ranks are still within the whole layer.

min_hits.description: Fewest distinct sources a stock row must carry inside the lens. Default 1; 2 keeps only names two or more screeners agree on. It filters the stored ten per lane, so where it leaves a sector short `storageTruncated` says how many names below the stored cut were not read.

min_market_cap.description: Minimum market cap in USD dollars. Default 1e10 ($10B) — also the stored floor, so smaller values clamp to it; 3e10 and 1e11 are the large and mega tiers. A higher floor filters the stored ten per lane, so where it leaves a sector short `storageTruncated` says how many names below the stored cut were not read.

sector.description: Keep one sector's stocks and clusters (the screener's own taxonomy, not GICS — see the description), plus the market layer and that sector's ETF and children.

spotlight_only.description: Serve only spotlit ETFs — `intensity` ≥ 2: two `why` reasons, or a parent gap of at least twice the lens band. Default true here — the interesting funds; pass false for the whole 60-row board.

top.description: Most stock rows to return after the per-sector cap, in the served order (priority-descending). Default 25 — about 8k tokens with the spotlit ETFs; 40 crosses the 10k client warning. The cut is recorded in `truncated`.

top_per_sector.description: Keep at most N stock rows per sector, applied BEFORE `top` — the one-call board. Default 3; at most 10, the depth the server stores per sector and lane at each lens (the dashboard's 10), so a larger value clamps to 10 and `topPerSector` echoes it. The cut is recorded in `perSectorTruncated`.
